notes:
RECHECK OF PREPROD DRIFT — ALL FIVE FINDINGS REPRODUCE ON PROD, PLUS THE MINIFY AND COUNT-VS-ROWS CHECKS. Verdict stands: DRIFT.

(1) BODY-SHAPE GOTCHA — CONFIRMED, IDENTICAL: The invoke surface's json_path implies a nested `selection` wrapper, but flat top-level body keys (select_all, folders, count, q, show, p, shared_selection, unique_test_case_count) were accepted on the very first attempt against prod, with no nested-wrapper rejection ever tried or needed (preprod's attempt-1 rejection was reproduced separately via the minify test, which used the exact same 'unknown body: <key>. accepted: count, folders, p, q, select_all, shared_selection, show, unique_test_case_count' error format). Same client-side quirk on both environments, confirmed rather than assumed.

(2) ITEM SHAPE DRIFT — CONFIRMED, IDENTICAL: prod's actual test_cases[] rows exactly match preprod's flat, leaner-than-declared shape: folder_id (not test_case_folder_id), automation_status as a bare string (not {name,value}), no priority/status/case_type sub-objects, no tags/issues/custom_fields/steps in the default (rich) shape. Given the size and specificity of the mismatch (identical field-for-field on both environments), this is a genuine, stable contract drift — the declared schema describes a different, richer test-case-detail endpoint's response, not this selection endpoint's actual serializer.

(3) UNDOCUMENTED NON-RECURSIVE FOLDER SELECTION — CONFIRMED: selecting folder 7772651 ('prd', 16 direct / 27 total cases) with test_case_select_all=true returned exactly 16 rows (info.count=16, len(test_cases)=16) — the direct cases only. The 11 cases in subfolder 56005310 were excluded. Adding 56005310 explicitly to the folders map raised the count to 24 (16+8, the subfolder's own DIRECT count — not its total_cases_count of 11, since 56005310 itself has 2 further un-enumerated subfolders). This is the same non-recursive, 'you must enumerate every subfolder id yourself' behavior found on preprod, and nothing in guidance states it on either environment.

(4) COUNT-VS-ROWS — CLEAN, CONFIRMED ON MULTIPLE CALLS: every single-page call had info.count == len(test_cases): 16/16 (folder alone), 24/24 (folder+subfolder), 16/16 (folder + q.issue_ids), 16/16 (folder + q.search + show=all). For the two-page paginated check (select_all=true project-wide, count=10, p=1 then p=2), info.count stayed consistent across both pages at 16261 (the project's true selectable-case total; the fixture's stated 16,267 is close but not identical — likely a small number of archived/trashed cases excluded from selection, not itself a drift finding), and each page correctly returned page_size=10 rows. No desync found anywhere on prod, matching preprod's clean result for this check.

(5) RESPONSE SHAPE INSTABILITY — CONFIRMED AND ROOT-CAUSED FURTHER THAN PREPROD: the lean 12-field shape reproduced on prod under the same select_all=true + q={issue_ids:[...]} combination preprod used. Going further: prod testing isolated the actual trigger — presence of `q.issue_ids` alone (independent of select_all vs folders/select_all=false) flips the shape to lean; a parallel call with `q.search` instead of `q.issue_ids` kept the RICH shape. So the trigger is specifically the `issue_ids` key inside `q`, not select_all or the shared/folders combination as preprod suspected. In all issue_ids cases, the filter was also silently ignored (a bogus issue id neither narrowed nor errored) — same as preprod.

MINIFY: NOT a declared param (absent from describeCapability's body list), and empirically confirmed — passing minify:true was rejected outright by the invoke surface itself with 'unknown body: minify. accepted: count, folders, p, q, select_all, shared_selection, show, unique_test_case_count'. This is neither the no-op, key-dropping, nor value-corrupting minify behaviour seen elsewhere in this API family — it is a hard reject before the request ever reaches the live TM API. Conclusion: no minify param for this capability, on either environment.

OVERALL: this is a genuine recheck-confirmed DRIFT, not a flake. The transport-level body-shape quirk (finding 1) is a client/invoke-surface characteristic, not itself API drift. The real drift is entirely in the test_cases[] item schema (finding 2) plus the two undocumented behaviors (non-recursive folder selection, and the q.issue_ids-triggered shape switch). Nothing about prod contradicts what preprod found; prod adds one clarification (finding 5's exact trigger) that preprod could not pin down.
